prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (alias/call sign Juniper) is the region’s primary dispatch and coordination point. It handles calls, creates incident records, coordinates jurisdictions, dispatches ambulances, and maintains shared incident, unit, access, zone-coverage, and availability information under approved protocols. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local-policy responsibility; zones/routes are maintained with them and reviewed as conditions change. Actors/elements: Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur) confirms location before medical details, gathers location, callback, patient condition/symptoms, onset, and access information, repeats/checks location, updates records with new information before dispatch decisions, and produces Caller Location Correction Slip when needed. Regional Dispatch Center preserves original reports alongside clarifications, distinguishing confirmed details from estimates. Clinical triage begins after symptoms, location, and immediate hazards are captured; recorded information is an initial basis, not a substitute for reassessment. Triage Supervisor (operational alias Copperfield) reviews uncertain/conflicting/rapidly deteriorating cases, directs focused clarification without delaying urgent response, assigns priority by threat, time sensitivity, and deterioration risk, and escalates ambiguous/severe cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits. Immediate threats receive highest available priority and prompt dispatch; other cases are prioritized by expected harm from delay and condition. Triage Supervisor sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy and guidance; does not hold operational dispatch authority. Shift Commander (Sundial) coordinates operations/continuity, surge priorities, readiness, and escalation; does not supersede clinical policy or Paramedic Crew scene judgment. Paramedic Crew provides scoped care, reports barriers/readiness, and verifies routes. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network and backup/coverage checks. Ambulance Coordination Platform presents incidents, assignments, status, coverage; Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks location against address/map data, which staff verify current. Ambulance Unit 417 joins pool when assigned. Hospital Liaison Desk (coordination alias Kestrel) confirms facility capabilities/contact paths, checks destination preferences against capability, records constraints in incident notes, shares current facility information without delaying intake, and produces Bedside Arrival Receipt on confirmed ambulance arrival. Emergency Department communicates constraints; Riverside Trauma Center is designated. North/South Gate Status Boards show access; North Gate Status Board produces North Approach Queue Snapshot. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors availability/service/defects and produces Battery Swap Voucher. Data Quality Officer (alias Pebble) checks records for gaps, inconsistencies,

New part:
S089: Data Quality Officer flags data defects for review but does not independently change a clinical priority.
S090: Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents the current incident details and assigned priority to authorized dispatch staff.
S091: Ambulance Coordination Platform uses the recorded priority alongside unit availability and operational constraints when coordinating response resources.
S092: Radio Coordinator communicates dispatch instructions and priority changes over Regional Radio Network.
S093: Paramedic Crew reports material changes in patient condition so that the incident can be reassessed promptly.
S094: Ambulance Unit 417 follows the active dispatch instructions and requests clarification when the incident details do not support safe response.
S095: Emergency Department may provide operationally relevant capacity information, while clinical triage remains governed by approved regional protocols.
S096: Riverside Trauma Center is considered for destination coordination when the patient's needs and current clinical guidance support that option.
S097: Shift Commander is notified when competing high-priority incidents exceed available response capacity or require an operational exception.
S098: Data Quality Officer reviews whether priority changes and their supporting rationale are recorded consistently for later assessment.
S099: Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S100: Triage Supervisor reviews significant disagreements about urgency and records the basis for the final operational priority.
S101: Resource selection begins after the operational priority and essential response requirements have been confirmed.
S102: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents units whose reported status and capabilities match the incident requirements.
S103: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays estimated travel times, unit availability, and relevant access constraints.
S104: The Triage Supervisor confirms that the selected response level remains consistent with the caller information.
S105: The selection decision weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle capability, crew readiness, and regional coverage.
S106: The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides current information about vehicles that are unavailable or restricted.
S107: The Radio Coordinator checks that the proposed unit can be reached on the Regional Radio Network.
S108: A dispatcher may recommend a unit, but dispatch authorization must follow the current regional approval rules.
S109: The Shift Commander approves exceptions that would materially reduce local coverage or require a nonstandard response.
S110: The Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical resource requirements when the incident presents an unusual care need.
S111: The dispatcher records the authorized unit and any conditions attached to its assignment.
S112: Regional Dispatch Center produces the Unit Staging Change Card when a previously selected unit must be repositioned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
